scenes.title: A new trust boundary
scenes.narration: AI systems increasingly interpret content from audio, files, and external services. Security teams need controlled ways to study how untrusted inputs are perceived and handled.

scenes.title: A defensive research framework
scenes.narration: Siren-Trap is an open-source Python research prototype for defensive AI red teaming and multimodal security evaluation, using controlled acoustic test artifacts and inert canary markers.

scenes.title: Observe, measure, evaluate
scenes.narration: The framework combines fixed canary generation, a localhost-first instrumented decoy service, structured telemetry, and passive analysis of recorded WAV files in a defined frequency band.

scenes.title: Controlled experiments
scenes.narration: The design favors inert test markers, bounded observations, and explicit authorization. The analyzer measures signal energy; it does not transmit audio, execute agent instructions, or prove that an agent can be controlled.

scenes.title: Research value
scenes.narration: Security researchers can use the framework to structure repeatable experiments, inspect trust-boundary behavior, and collect evidence that helps teams evaluate defensive handling of multimodal inputs.

scenes.title: Alpha research prototype
scenes.narration: Siren-Trap does not certify physical-layer performance or production containment. Hardware compatibility, verified end-to-end decoding, and reproducible benchmark adapters remain to be completed. Read the threat model and responsible-use guidance on GitHub.
